indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of the word paternal might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A tentative suggestion that something is fatherly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' does two things at once: it shows paternal is only one example of the answer, and it signals that the same letters can be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatherly feelings are one kind of the feelings belonging to a mother or father.

clue.text: Make request and get into trouble

explanation.surface: Someone who asks for something and lands in hot water.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means to make a demand, and idiomatically means to invite trouble by provoking it.

clue.text: Jack gets lines for naughty behaviour

parts.note: the jack in a pack of cards is also called the knave
RY, short for railway, stands for lines (railway lines)

explanation.surface: A boy called Jack is given lines as a punishment for misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a boy's name and 'lines' like a school punishment of writing out sentences; in fact they are the playing card and the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Roguish trickery or mischief is the conduct of a rascal.

indicators.note: to enter means the word for fit goes inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: fit in the sense of healthy and well, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: A building suitable for use as a courthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like an adjective meaning suitable, but it means healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss-style wooden cottage or holiday cabin is a kind of dwelling.

parts.note: men, a general word for people
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A guide leading a party of walkers up a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a rocky hilltop, common in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A trusted adviser or counsellor steers a less experienced person.

indicators.note: qualified in the sense of modified or altered, so the letters of whole lameness are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether total immobility entitles someone to a home food-delivery service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'qualified' reads as 'eligible', but it signals the rearrangement of WHOLE LAMENESS; the whole clue also describes who receives the service.
explanation.definitionFit: A British service delivering hot food to the housebound, often elderly or disabled people.

parts.note: stuff as a noun means fabric or substance, material
to sing is to celebrate in song

explanation.surface: Someone arriving with supplies and in a festive mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Appearing or coming into being, as a ghost suddenly shows up.

parts.note: second prize is the silver medal, and a prize for oratory is earned by the tongue, so a speaker winning one has a silver tongue

explanation.surface: A speech judged good enough to come runner-up in a public-speaking contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Being persuasive and eloquent in speech is like having a precious-metal voice.

clue.text: The actual thing is left off

indicators.note: off in the sense of out of order or wrong, so the letters of is left are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that has been left out of the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' reads as 'omitted', but it signals the rearrangement of IS LEFT.
explanation.definitionFit: The reflexive pronoun stresses the very object in question, as in 'the house itself'.

explanation.surface: Describing a scatterbrained person who now and then chases someone called Sal.
explanation.walkthrough: SAL VOLATILE is smelling salts, once used to revive people who fainted, so the word sometimes follows 'Sal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fickle and changeable people are unpredictable; the word also completes the name of smelling salts.

clue.text: Nothing you and I have as debt

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
you and I together are we

explanation.surface: A couple with no savings who are in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in debt to someone is to be obliged to pay them.

parts.note: an old crate is slang for a battered old car
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An old banger of a car drives into a huge hole in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs into' suggests a crash, but R simply follows CRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bowl-shaped hollow in the ground, as left by an explosion.

clue.text: Cake eaten by Socialist had been thrown back

indicators.note: eaten by means the word for cake goes inside the word for socialist

parts.note: red is a common word for a socialist or communist
a torte is a rich layered cake

explanation.surface: A left-winger has eaten a cake that was earlier thrown back.
explanation.definitionFit: Answering sharply in kind, as a remark is flung back at the speaker.

parts.note: the cry of approval a Spanish speaker uses for 'bravo', heard at bullfights and flamenco

explanation.surface: Praising someone for speaking Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish exclamation of approval or encouragement, like bravo.

parts.note: pal is an informal word for friend
lets as a verb means rents out or hires

explanation.surface: A friend rents out the platforms used for loading goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat wooden frames on which goods are stacked for moving by forklift.

indicators.note: chosen from means the letters are picked out of the word several

explanation.surface: A girl selected from a group of candidates.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, that of the first woman in the Bible.

clue.text: Problem with body needing fast cure

definitions.text: Problem with body needing fast cure

parts.words: Problem with body needing fast cure
parts.note: a bodily condition seemingly needing a quick remedy, but the cure is fasting, going without food

explanation.surface: A medical complaint requiring a quick remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like 'quick', but it means abstaining from food.
explanation.definitionFit: Being severely overweight is a health condition treated by eating less.

clue.text: In card game, good skill he boasts

parts.note: brag is a British card game similar to poker
art means skill or craft

explanation.surface: A card player who brags about his skill at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAG is a traditional British card game, a forerunner of poker.
explanation.definitionFit: A boaster is someone who is always showing off.

clue.text: The most one has to bowl?

definitions.text: The most one has to bowl?

parts.words: The most one has to bowl?
parts.note: bowl reads like a cricket verb, but it is the hollow part of a spoon, and this is all the bowl of one spoon holds

explanation.surface: A cricketer asking the maximum number of balls he must deliver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowl' suggests cricket, where a bowler delivers the ball, but here it is the hollow of a spoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure of food or medicine filling the scoop of a single spoon.

indicators.note: incomplete means the word for poetry loses its final letter

parts.note: verse is a word for poetry
an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: Half-finished poetry is charged for as a translation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts the last E from VERSE to leave VERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendering of a text into another language, such as the King James Bible.

clue.text: By lake, Heather slips, for example

parts.note: ling is a common heather
Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A woman named Heather slips over beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name and 'slips' like a fall; they are the plant and petticoats. Heather is placed by the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Slips are petticoats, one kind of women's underwear.

clue.text: Almost lose sight of unpleasant imp

indicators.note: almost means the phrase for lose sight is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to go blind is to lose one's sight

explanation.surface: Nearly losing sight of a nasty little demon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the final D of GO BLIND.
explanation.definitionFit: A malicious small creature of folklore, a mischievous sprite.

indicators.note: to edit means the letters of Greene are revised into a new order

explanation.surface: An editor refusing to touch the novelist Graham Greene's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greene' looks like the novelist Graham Greene, but it is only letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back on a promise or decline to honour a deal.

explanation.surface: Estimating what someone buys at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pubs one person buys drinks for the whole group, a round; split, the answer reads as 'a round'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means approximately; split in two it names a set of drinks for everyone.

explanation.surface: Cancelling a charity event.
explanation.walkthrough: At British universities a rag is a students' charity fund-raising week of stunts.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a tatter of cloth; a students' charity carnival also goes by this name.

parts.note: breaking up groups of musicians, but the word means to break up any organised body

explanation.surface: Breaking up groups of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking up a group or regiment; read playfully, undoing musical groups.

clue.text: High-IQ type I put into division of class

indicators.note: put into means the letter I is placed inside the word for a division of class

parts.note: in biology a class is divided into orders, families and genera

explanation.surface: Someone with a high IQ is placed in a top school set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class' looks like a school class, but in biology a genus is a group within a class.
explanation.definitionFit: An exceptionally clever person, a brilliant mind.

clue.text: Setting off for game get hiding

explanation.surface: Leaving for a match and getting a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' looks like a beating; it means concealment. A ground is a sports stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading to the stadium for a match; also, like a fox into its earth, vanishing from sight.
